We then evaluated a few papers, examining the technologies used and their advantages, key focuses, and limitations. This survey aims to determine the potential of blockchain technology in improving transaction efficiency, transparency, cost reduction, and other beneficial aspects of rental management. Blockchain technology is a workable alternative to traditional rental lease management, streamlining processes, building confidence, and asserting the dynamics between landlords and tenants. This paper addresses a survey in different domains of application of blockchain technology and some suggestions for future research.

articleTitle: Wheat Powdery Mildew Automatic Identification Through YOLOv8 Instance Segmentation
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Reliability, Infocom Technologies and Optimization (Trends and Future Directions) (ICRITO)
abstract: The global production of wheat is seriously endangered by wheat powdery mildew, which can be brought on by Blumeria graminis f. sp. tritici (Bgt). The illness produces large annual losses and threatens food security. The labourintensive and time-consuming characteristics of conventional detection methods emphasizes the need for elegant, automated surveillance systems. Deep learning techniques, particularly the YOLOv8 instance segmentation model, were employed in this study to enhance wheat powdery mildew detection and classification. Results indicate the YOLOv8 model is efficient; it can recognize wheat leaves affected by powdery mildew with a precision of 99.37%, recall of 96%, and an F1-score of 97.67%. This approach works superior to before methods, making it a promising solution for early detection of illnesses in wheat crops. In addition, the research's next steps are examined, highlighting the potential of improving the YOLOv8 model in an array of environmental situations and disease stages. Effective disease detection could be enhanced by merging new data sources as drone-based monitoring systems and hyperspectral imaging. Developing and setting up autonomous disease tracking systems in real agricultural settings involves collaboration among data scientists, technologists, and agronomic teams, in addition to user-friendly interfaces tailored to farmer needs. When everything is taken into account, this study promotes the development of successful tools to control diseases, promoting sustainable crop production and assuring food safety around the globe.

articleTitle: Use of OLS Regression Model as Predictor to Compute Excessive Returns in ESM
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Reliability, Infocom Technologies and Optimization (Trends and Future Directions) (ICRITO)
abstract: Open Offer events are helpful for investors to obtain the necessary sustainable wealth with the aid of cutting-edge machine learning algorithms. Open Offer is a statutory instrument for the firms to achieve the desired ownership in the target companies. The focus of the current analysis was the 697 open offer occasions for businesses. The Stock Exchange of Bombay was the listing place. The research ran from 2019 to 2023 for five years. The final prediction analysis for sustainable wealth generation on 229 organizations was done after the first investigation, which used the standardized event research approach. The criteria for inclusion and exclusion were utilized. The report's data gathering processes for each organization used a range of statistical techniques, such as Abnormal by applying the inclusion-exclusion criteria. To calculate the wealth in the event window, the study utilized a variety of statistical procedures, such as average abnormal returns, cumulative average of unacceptable returns, total of unusual returns, and to the data set of each individual firm independently. On the other hand, several tests, including the BMP, Patell Z, Corrado, T, and sign tests, were used to evaluate hypotheses to look at noteworthy findings for sustainable wealth. The study discovered substantial and long-term wealth production in the majority of Open Offer events, which empowers minority investors

articleTitle: Optimizing Stress Detection: Harnessing MobileNet-V2 with Azimuthal EEG Mapping
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Reliability, Infocom Technologies and Optimization (Trends and Future Directions) (ICRITO)
abstract: This investigation meticulously assesses stress classification models using benchmark datasets (D1, D2, D3). The study delves into the effectiveness of models, notably MobileNet-V2, incorporating an innovative Azimuthal Projection approach. MobileNet-V2 consistently outshines its counterparts, showcasing impressive accuracy, specificity, sensitivity, and F1 Score. Noteworthy achievements include 95.5% accuracy, 98.8% specificity, and 95.5% sensitivity on D1, with a mere 3.5-hour training time. In D2 and D3, MobileNet-V2 maintains excellence with 96% accuracy, 97.5% specificity, and 96% sensitivity, emphasizing its computational efficiency with training times of 3.8 hours on D2 and 3.6 hours on D3. These findings position MobileNet-V2, integrated with Azimuthal Projection, as the preferred choice for stress classification, effectively balancing performance and resource utilization.

articleTitle: An Extensive Analysis on Intelligent Methods for Sheet Metal Processes
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Reliability, Infocom Technologies and Optimization (Trends and Future Directions) (ICRITO)
abstract: Intelligent sheet metal processes have revolutionized the manufacturing industry, offering greater efficiency, precision, and cost-effectiveness. These processes leverage advanced technologies such as Artificial Intelligence (AI) techniques i.e. Machine Learning (ML) approaches, Knowledge Based Systems (KBS) and Computer-Aided Design (CAD) software to optimize various aspects of sheet metal fabrication. By harnessing the power of these technologies, manufacturers can automate and streamline their sheet metal processes in ways that were previously unimaginable. In this paper, an extensive analysis of the intelligent sheet metal processes is presented to explore how they are being utilized to enhance these processes. We analyze the benefits and challenges associated with implementing intelligent sheet metal processes, including improved accuracy, reduced cycle times, and enhanced product quality. Through this paper, we aim to provide a holistic understanding of intelligent sheet metal processes and their potential for transforming the manufacturing industry. In addition, we discuss future research directions and potential applications of intelligent sheet metal processes, paving the way for further advancements in this field.

articleTitle: Improving Insider Threat Detection with User and Role-Based Behavior
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Reliability, Infocom Technologies and Optimization (Trends and Future Directions) (ICRITO)
abstract: Insider threats are a growing concern for organizations, and existing methods have fallen short in their ability to detect these threats effectively. One significant constraint of current techniques is their inability to discern between the conduct of malicious users and that of their counterparts in identical job roles. But these methods did not use features that show how different a user's behavior is from that of their peers in the same job role. This study aims to detect insider threats by analyzing the user and roles that may involve in malicious activity. Malicious users can be identified by extracting different features that describe their activities and how they differ from those of their peers. The Isolation Forest Algorithm is an unsupervised method that compares each user's variance across many attributes with those of their peers in order to identify abnormalities. The performance of the proposed approach is thoroughly evaluated through a series of experiments conducted. The results of the comparison between the proposed method and a current state-of-the-art technique confirm's that the proposed detection method is more reliable.

articleTitle: IoT-Enabled Facial Recognition for Smart Hospitality for Contactless Guest Services and Identity Verification
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Reliability, Infocom Technologies and Optimization (Trends and Future Directions) (ICRITO)
abstract: The proposed system integrates face recognition and Internet of Things (IoT) technology to revolutionize the hospitality industry. It uses OpenCV, a widely recognized computer vision library, to deliver smooth, contactless guest services and rigorous identification verification. This paper proposes a novel method to improve visitor experiences by removing check-in and allowing personalized services. The IoT -enabled face recognition system presented in this paper streamlines the visitor experiences. Facial biometrics eliminates the need for identity papers, making the check-in process simple. The proposed system, OpenCV, is used for face detection, identification, and verification. The system's design includes strategically positioned cameras for visitor identification and tracking. Health and safety are crucial, so this system's contactless nature is a major benefit. The solution also increases visitor safety by lowering the danger of fraud and illegal access. The IoT-enabled face recognition technology improves operational efficiency, guest satisfaction, and security in the hospital industry.

articleTitle: An Approach to Recognize Efficient Deep Learning Model for Pattern Recognition
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Reliability, Infocom Technologies and Optimization (Trends and Future Directions) (ICRITO)
abstract: Pattern recognition using deep learning is one of the earliest and prevailing computer vision tasks and is a frequently used research area in today's world. Deep Learning methods are currently being used in numerous applications such as Video and speech recognition, Computer Vision tasks, cybernetics, text mining, financial fraud detection, etc. DL is derived from classical neural networks which improvises them extensively. Recently developed DL algorithms have achieved excellent performance in various applications mentioned above. Despite the successful use of deep learning models in numerous domains, constructing a suitable deep learning model remains a difficult job. This difficulty arises from the dynamic and diverse nature of real-world issues and inputs. This paper emphasizes recent developments in deep learning, types of DL techniques, its applications and further highlights the challenges and findings to ease researchers in identifying research needs in the area of pattern recognition.

articleTitle: Global Perspectives in Facial Recognition for Cyber Security: A Bibliometeric Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Reliability, Infocom Technologies and Optimization (Trends and Future Directions) (ICRITO)
abstract: This research paper presents a comprehensive bibliometric analysis unveiling insights into the global landscape of research in facial recognition for cyber security. Leveraging data from 12,073 publications, the study explores the contributions of various countries and regions, shedding light on the collaborative and diverse nature of this dynamic field. Notably, the people's Republic of China emerges as a leading contributor, closely followed by the United States and the United Kingdom. The Asian region, including India, Saudi Arabia, and South Korea, demonstrates significant participation, while diverse contribution from European nations further enriches the global research tapestry. The findings underscore the truly international character of facial recognition research for cyber security, emphasizing the need for ongoing collaboration ton address emerging challenges and advance the field.

articleTitle: Comprehensive Performance Assessment of Machine Learning Techniques in NIFTY-50 Stock Index Prediction
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Reliability, Infocom Technologies and Optimization (Trends and Future Directions) (ICRITO)
abstract: In the ever-changing landscape of global finance, the precise forecasting of stock indices has emerged as a pivotal concern for both investors and financial analysts. This study explores the effectiveness of multiple machine learning (ML) based techniques, including Linear Regression (LR), Support Vector Regression (SVR), Adaboost, Random Forrest (RF) and Feedforward Neural Network (FNN), implemented within the MATLAB framework. MATLAB, a versatile and powerful platform, is employed for deploying and evaluating predictive models. Adaboost, known for its ensemble learning approach, iteratively combines weak learners to construct a robust prediction model. Simultaneously, model optimization is achieved through techniques such as grid search. The study utilizes several technical indicators calculated from the historical NIFTY-50 index data to train and validate the predictive models. Performance metrics such as RMSE, MAE, MAPE, R2 errors are employed to evaluate the efficacy of the algorithms. The research results contribute to the growing knowledge base in financial prediction, showcasing the practical application of ML techniques within the MATLAB Software framework. The results not only provide a basis for improved predictions in the NIFTY-50 index but also offer valuable insights for future research in the domain of algorithmic trading and financial market analysis.

articleTitle: Fault Prediction of Agile-Based Software Using Attention-Based BiGRU
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Reliability, Infocom Technologies and Optimization (Trends and Future Directions) (ICRITO)
abstract: Software reliability is a critical concern in various industries, where failures can lead to severe consequences. Agile development, particularly under the Agile Framework (SAFe), has gained prominence for managing large-scale projects. However, there is a limited focus on predicting software reliability within an agile context. Existing models often treat each sprint independently, overlooking cumulative effects. This research introduces a fault prediction model for SAFe-based systems, utilising a Bi-Directional Gated Recurrent Unit (BiGRU) and a self-attention mechanism. BiGRU considers past and future sprints, addressing the shortcomings of traditional models. The self-attention mechanism enhances the model's ability to capture dependencies between sprints. The proposed approach demonstrates its effectiveness through a practical example. This research offers a more accurate and comprehensive strategy for anticipating and managing software faults in agile, large-scale industrial applications.

articleTitle: Internet of Things for Home Management and Control
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Reliability, Infocom Technologies and Optimization (Trends and Future Directions) (ICRITO)
abstract: The concept of home automation is applied with the help of the Internet of Things (IoT). There was a time when people used to operate home automation with the help of Bluetooth without any help from the internet. In today's fast-paced world, the utility of automated homes, mobile devices, digitally enhanced cities, and digital timepieces has been adopted very easily, or it can be said that it has given more simplicity to human life. This study proposes to manage our home with home automation technology through the Internet of Things. Smart appliances and home appliances can also be controlled from a distance. The concept of home automation is associated with the IoT. The connected device network is a technology by which two or more device are interconnected with each other so that communication can be established between them. Human intervention instructs the machinery and instruments. It controls home appliances and electronics equipment through the internet, such as web sites or smart phones. The basic goal of IoT for home management and control is to improve human daily lives by making it more efficient and convenient to use household items and reducing the need for manual intervention.

articleTitle: An Augmented Approach to Vehicle - Type Classification using Deep Transfer Learning Approaches with adam Optimizer
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Reliability, Infocom Technologies and Optimization (Trends and Future Directions) (ICRITO)
abstract: Intelligent Transportation Systems (ITS) for an Internet of Things (IoT) Smart City are primarily concerned with enhancing the safety, efficiency via information and communication technology. It is vital to have systems in place that can gather road data and monitor traffic. In this research, we used data from the Stanford AI automobile dataset, where we were tasked with classifying 196 vehicles. We employed deep transfer learning algorithms, including ResNet50, MobileNetV2, and DenseNet169. This study offers a technique to enhance the detection of occluded vehicles. Due to the increased traffic & number of cars to classify that resulted in blockage or occlusion, we applied the ADAM (adaptive moment estimation) optimizer approach to obtain the best results. The results are assessed for both the training & validation phases based on accuracy, precision, root mean square error, loss, recall & Fl score. During the training phase, DenseNet169 scored the best accuracy (99.83%), highest recall (95.46%), lowest loss (0.01), and rmse value (0.10) & 97.89<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup> precision, 95.46% recall, and 90.59% Fl score during validation phase.

articleTitle: Future Prospects of ChatGPT in Higher Education
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Reliability, Infocom Technologies and Optimization (Trends and Future Directions) (ICRITO)
abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) has been found to solve complex problems in education sector. AI enabled chatbots and virtual assistants have been found to support the higher education institutions (HEls) in their academic and non-academic work. Users of ChatGPT has been phenomenally increasing in developing countries like India. Therefore, an in-depth and insightful research among academicians is required to comprehend the role of ChatGPT in higher education in India. This research paper attempts to explore the role of ChatGPT in future of higher education in India. The research was directed at faculties in higher education institutions (HEls) in Tier I cities in India. The authors conducted purposive sampling and applied Interpretative Phenomenological Analysis (IP A) among respondents. The research findings reveal that ChatGPT has immense role to play in higher education. However, looking into the pros and cons of ChatGPT, higher education institutions need to train their students on ethical usage of this tool. Moreover, they need to train their teachers to act as facilitators and use ChatGPT as an innovative pedagogical tool in their teaching and assessment.

articleTitle: Agricultural Intelligence: Federated Learning CNN's Models for Jute Leaf Disease Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Reliability, Infocom Technologies and Optimization (Trends and Future Directions) (ICRITO)
abstract: The research study performs an experimental analysis of a federated learning system that uses convolutional neural networks (CNNs) to detect and classify jute leaf diseases from many distributed data sources. We focus on five specific categories of jute leaf diseases, using local datasets from five individual clients to generate personalized models. The models are ensembled using federated averaging to create a robust global algorithm. Federated learning harnesses privacy and data security but enables the model to learn from various illness symptoms. The findings are promising, indicating that the federated learning model not only preserves but also improves the accuracy of illness categorization when moved from local to global data sets. The model's performance was assessed using precision, recall, F1-score, support, and accuracy parameters. The average accuracy, recall, and F1score increased from 78.86%, 78.7%, and 78.71% for mq_1 to 94.21%, 94.19%, and 94.2% for mq_5 for the five clients. The weighted means showed a similar improvement, with mq_1 starting at 79.38% and mq_5 reaching 94.22%. Micro averages had the same trend of increase, growing from 79.27% for mq_1 to 94.22% for mq_5. The statistical measures reveal increasing diagnostic precision of the model as the federated learning process advances. The research also examines the performance of federated averaging in aggregating local data sets for a global model. The global model accuracy achieves the best accuracy of local clients, up to 0.98. This shows how federated learning improves the global model by adding local data contributions. The research emphasizes the efficiency of federated learning and CNNs in solving the complex problem of jute leaf disease classification.

articleTitle: A Comparative Analysis of Bias Mitigation Methods in Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Reliability, Infocom Technologies and Optimization (Trends and Future Directions) (ICRITO)
abstract: Fairness in AI and Machine Learning is gaining traction everyday as more people are understanding the profound effects it can have on a model's predictions. While there is scope for advancement in this field, multiple bias mitigation methods and fairness metrics have already been developed. This study aims to conduct a comparative analysis of different bias mitigation techniques using the UCI Adult Income dataset while deploying Logistic Regression as the base model. This study focuses solely on analyzing technical methods to mitigate bias, excluding non-technical approaches. One of pre-processing, in-processing, and post-processing methods are chosen and implemented for analysis using Python and the AI Fairness 360 (AIF360) toolkit. We evaluate the model's predictions before and after debiasing, and we use fairness and classification metrics to compare the impact of different bias mitigation strategies. Additionally, statistical tests are utilized to determine if the methods make any significant differences.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Fuzzy based Controller for Lane Keeping Assistance
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Reliability, Infocom Technologies and Optimization (Trends and Future Directions) (ICRITO)
abstract: Lane-keeping assistance control is a critical aspect of autonomous vehicle technology, aimed at ensuring the safety and stability of vehicles on the road. This research focuses on the development and comparative analysis of three distinct fuzzy based logic designs for lane-keeping assistance. The proposed controllers utilize different combinations of input parameters, including lateral deviation, yaw error, and speed, to generate the optimal steering angle for maintaining the vehicle within the lane. This study evaluates and compares three fuzzy logic controllers (FLC): Fuzz-Con-I, Fuzz-Con-II, and Fuzz-Con-III. Fuzz-Con-I uses lateral deviation and velocity to control the steering angle. Fuzz-Con-II employs yaw Error and velocity for the same purpose, while Fuzz-Con-Iii integrates lateral deviation, yaw error, and velocity. The performance of these FLCs is systematically analyzed and compared against state feedback and fuzzy PID control strategies. The simulation experiments employed a vehicle model, specifically depicted as a single tracked bicycle model, created within the MATLAB/SIMULINK environment. This model was regarded as a dynamic system with vision, and various control logics were applied and tested during the experiments.

articleTitle: Next-Generation Tele-Communication Networks and IoT: Advancements and Challenges
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Reliability, Infocom Technologies and Optimization (Trends and Future Directions) (ICRITO)
abstract: The speedy advancement of generation has transformed the conventional tile-communication networks into next-era networks, incorporating new features and skills to fulfill the needs of the digital technology. The emergence of the Iota has also revolutionized the tele-communique landscape by connecting gadgets and items to the net, enabling seamless conversation and data exchange. It has opened up new opportunities to improve innovative offerings and applications. The key advancements in subsequent-technology tile-verbal exchange networks and Iota encompass progressed connectivity, stronger information speeds, and higher network ability. Those networks also allow the combination of various conversation technologies consisting of 5G, cloud computing, and artificial intelligence, delivering advanced services like digital and augmented fact. Moreover, the implementation of network slicing and network automation in addition enhances those networks' performance and overall performance.

articleTitle: Revolutionizing Vehicle Safety: IOT-Enabled Inter Vehicular Communication for Real-time Data Transfer and Emergency Response Via Wi-Fi
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Reliability, Infocom Technologies and Optimization (Trends and Future Directions) (ICRITO)
abstract: The integration of Internet technology has led to the seamless incorporation of cloud computing into automotive systems, resulting in the development of autonomous vehicles known for enhanced efficiency and robust security. Through the utilization of Wireless Fidelity (Wi-Fi) technology, intervehicular communication has been established, employing internet proto- cols as the conduit for the real-time transmission of diverse sensor data between two vehicles. This exchange forms the basis for intelligent decision-making processes, with Node Microcontroller unit (NodeMCU) chipsets serving as integral components in the intricate framework. Operative within the 2.4GHz frequency spectrum, these chipsets facilitate the expeditious transfer and real-time processing of data, demonstrating the mechanisms that yield visual outputs through seamless integration with cloud infrastructure. The outcomes yielded were both efficacious and precise, evincing a seamless data transfer devoid of any latency. The two chipsets demonstrated facile data transmission through a cloud-based repository, amenable to simultaneous access by a tertiary chipset. Real-time inputs and outputs conformed meticulously to external environmental conditions, validating the anticipated efficacy of the proposed model. Leveraging Wi-Fi technology provided the system with an encrypted channel for data transmission, thereby enhancing speed and resulting in rapid and accurate inter-vehicular responses. This strengthens security and expedites Cellular Vehicle-to-Everything (C- V2X) communication.

articleTitle: A Non-Invasive Multi-Parameter System for Feto-Maternal Well-Being Assessment and Telemonitoring
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Reliability, Infocom Technologies and Optimization (Trends and Future Directions) (ICRITO)
abstract: This study describes the feto-maternal care unit (FMCU), a real-time, stand-alone, non-invasive monitoring system that analyzes physiological signals collected from pregnant women both during and after labor to identify the health of the fetus and the mother. The FMCU is a prototype multichannel device made up of multiple biomedical sensors that are affixed to the body of expectant mother. These sensors gather physiological signals in real-time, including uterine contractions, fetal movement, heart rate, and respiration rate of the mother. A data acquisition device (NI myRIO) wirelessly records these fluctuations, which are then sent to a computer running NI LabVIEW software for additional sophisticated signal processing, feature extraction, and feto-maternal wellbeing assessment. As the proposed system is built on a wireless client-server architecture, it can collect and send data from several patients at once. An android application that runs on the internet is also designed to help patients synchronize their health data directly to the cloud, where a licensed doctor can access it for additional advanced diagnostics and consultation. Because the technology is non-invasive, affordable, and simple to use, pregnant women living in remote or impoverished locations can benefit from home-based health telemonitoring and avoid making frequent trips to a far-off clinic.

articleTitle: Smart Conversations: Enhancing User Engagement through NLP in IoT Environments
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Reliability, Infocom Technologies and Optimization (Trends and Future Directions) (ICRITO)
abstract: The integration of NLP into IoT settings has emerged as a revolutionary framework, providing consumers with a more intuitive and participatory experience. This study examines the capacity of NLP to improve user involvement in IoT ecosystems by facilitating intelligent interactions between people and linked objects. The exponential growth of IoT devices has resulted in a surge of data, necessitating the development of efficient and user-friendly interfaces to facilitate smooth interactions. NLP is crucial in connecting people and IoT devices by enabling the comprehension and production of language that resembles human communication. By adding NLP, IoT environments may give users with a conversational interface, allowing them to manage and monitor equipment with natural language instructions. This study focuses on doing a comprehensive examination of current NLP approaches and their suitability for use in IoT environments. This work examines the problems and potential of integrating NLP in various IoT situations. It specifically focuses on tackling concerns related to language variety, contextual comprehension, and the need for real-time processing. Moreover, the research examines the influence of intelligent dialogues on user involvement, highlighting the possibility of heightened user contentment, effectiveness, and availability. Case studies and practical examples demonstrate effective use of NLP in IoT applications.

articleTitle: A Fine-Tuned Convolutional Neural Network Model for Banana Leaf Disease Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Reliability, Infocom Technologies and Optimization (Trends and Future Directions) (ICRITO)
abstract: The use of Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) for early identification of banana leaf diseases is a significant advancement in the area of image recognition technology. The primary objective of the proposed work is to develop and implement a CNN model that is capable of reliably locating and recognising banana leaves in images. To implement this strategy, a huge dataset of labelled images of banana leaves are compiled. These images have been selected from Kaggle and preprocessed to ensure that they are both varied and regular. In the pre-processing step, the images have been transformed into identical sizes to be understood by the CNN model. The capabilities of CNNs to learn hierarchically are used to construct a multi-layered architecture that includes convolutional, pooling, and fully connected layers. As part of the training process for the model, the dataset is subjected to recurrent optimisation to reduce a predetermined loss function. The capability of the model to identify banana leaf diseases in a broad variety of images is put to the test and validated via a series of layers of the CNN model. It has been shown that CNN is capable of accurately locating banana leaf diseases by achieving an accuracy of 98.24% at epoch 20. Further, the loss of the model has been also identified as the lowest at epoch 20 as 0.2936. This ability has the potential to be useful in a variety of fields, including agriculture, cookery, and environmental awareness. The development and validation of this CNN model's ability to identify banana leaf disease is a significant advancement in the area of automated visual recognition systems. This model has the potential to be used in a wide variety of industries and organisational applications.

articleTitle: Personalized Smart Grocery Delivery with IoT Technology Using Collaborative Filtering Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Reliability, Infocom Technologies and Optimization (Trends and Future Directions) (ICRITO)
abstract: Personalized suggestions may enhance the use of online food shopping, an already popular and handy service. But data sparsity and scalability problems restrict the current recommendation systems rely on user-based collaborative filtering algorithms. Smart grocery delivery with personalized suggestions is proposed in this system using item-based collaborative filtering algorithms and Internet of Things (IoT) technologies. In the system, smart appliances like fridges and scales track food supplies and consumption, and then, according to the user's preferences, they automatically place purchases on internet platforms. It makes use of item-based collaborative filtering algorithms to examine other users' evaluations and purchase histories in order to provide the user with relevant and varied product recommendations. The method is tested on a real-world dataset and contrasted with collaborative filtering methods rely on user input. Techniques outperform the competition in terms of suggestion accuracy, variety, and coverage while simultaneously decreasing delivery time and costs. By implementing our strategy, not only can online grocery shopping be made more enjoyable for users, but it can also spur the growth of e-commerce and the IoT.

articleTitle: Mental Healthcare Chatbot Based on Custom Diagnosis Documents Using a Quantized Large Language Model
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Reliability, Infocom Technologies and Optimization (Trends and Future Directions) (ICRITO)
abstract: This research presents a novel retrieval-based question-answering (QA) framework utilizing LangChain's (version 0.1.6) modular architecture and Chainlit's (version 0.7.700) conversational interface. Our system efficiently handles PDF and directory documents, generates sentence embeddings with HuggingFace's pre-trained model, stores vectors in FAISS for fast search, employs the powerful CTransformers (version 0.2.27) with Llama-2-7B-Chat-GGUF model, and guides it with a custom prompt template for accurate and factual responses. The integrated Chainlit interface facilitates user interaction, demonstrating the framework's potential for knowledge-intensive domains like medical chatbots.

articleTitle: An Analysis Conducted Retrospectively on the Use: Artificial Intelligence in the Detection of Uterine Fibroid
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Reliability, Infocom Technologies and Optimization (Trends and Future Directions) (ICRITO)
abstract: The most frequent benign pelvic tumors in women of age of conception are uterine fibroids, sometimes referred to as leiomyomas. Ultrasonography is presently the first imaging modality utilized as clinical identification of uterine fibroids since it has a high degree of specificity and sensitivity and is less expensive and more widely accessible than CT and MRI examination. However, certain issues with ultrasound based uterine fibroid diagnosis persist. The main problem is the misunderstanding of pelvic and adnexal masses, as well as subplasmic and large fibroids. The specificity of fibroid detection is impacted by the existing absence of standardized image capture views and the variations in performance amongst various ultrasound machines. Furthermore, the proficiency and expertise of ultra sonographers determines the accuracy of the ultrasound diagnosis of uterine fibroids. In this work, we created a Deep convolutional neural networks (DCNN) model that automatically identifies fibroids in the uterus in ultrasound pictures, distinguishes between their presence and absence, and has been internally as well as externally validated in order to increase the reliability of the ultrasound examinations for uterine fibroids. Additionally, we investigated whether Deep convolutional neural networks model may help junior ultrasound practitioners perform better diagnostically by comparing it to eight ultrasound practitioners at different levels of experience.

articleTitle: Enhancing Diagnostic Accuracy Denoising Medical Imaging
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Reliability, Infocom Technologies and Optimization (Trends and Future Directions) (ICRITO)
abstract: Medical image processing is faced with the challenge of accurate diagnosis founded on image noise, blurriness, and lack of proper preprocessing. In this paper, our model introduced various denoising techniques in medical image processing, from customary methods like Non-Local Means and Wavelet-Based Denoising to modern approaches such as autoencoders and the resultant images classified using the U-Net architecture. Autoencoders, akin to smart filters, exhibit assurance in efficiently annihilating unwanted artifacts while holding essential image features. The model's primary goal is to leverage autoencoders to enhance the clarity and Precision of medical image data and address challenges originating from image copying and quality loss. By utilizing U-Net neural networks, this analysis achieved an accuracy of 97.15%, Precision (97.87%), and recall (96.67%).

articleTitle: A Smart Bin with Real-Time Monitoring and Garbage Level Tracking Using IoT
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Reliability, Infocom Technologies and Optimization (Trends and Future Directions) (ICRITO)
abstract: This paper presents a novel system for smart waste management using IoT technology. With the rapid growth of urban areas and population, proper waste management has become a crucial issue for maintaining a healthy environment. The proposed system utilizes weight sensors and ultrasonic transducers to monitor the fill levels of dust bins in real-time. The system provides a user-friendly web page that displays a visual representation of the garbage levels in each bin, allowing users to take appropriate actions based on the current status. The system also sorts trash according to their weight, providing a precise idea for transportation of products. The proposed system offers an innovative and advantageous approach to waste management, promoting efficient and sustainable practices.

articleTitle: FARMER: Forecasting Agricultural Results with Machine Learning Evaluation and Regression
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Reliability, Infocom Technologies and Optimization (Trends and Future Directions) (ICRITO)
abstract: Agriculture plays an important role, in Indias economy providing support to a portion of the population and contributing significantly to the GDP. It is crucial to predict crop yields in order to make decisions and promote sustainable agricultural practices. To achieve this a research study proposes an approach that utilizes machine learning techniques such as Decision Tree, Support Vector Machine (SVM) Random Forest, Multiple Linear Regression and Partial Least Squares Regression. The study carefully evaluates the performance of these models. Reveals some findings while comparing them to determine the best model. Multiple Linear Regression achieves the accuracy at 81.2% followed by Decision Tree at 83.5% SVM at 92.1% Random Forest at 91.5%. Partial Least Squares Regression at 85.3%. Notably SVM emerges as the performing model demonstrating its potential in improving precision, for predicting agricultural yields. Ultimately an Android application is developed using Kotlin and Android Studio for an user experience.

articleTitle: Virtual Illusions: Unleashing Deepfake Expertise for Enhanced Visual Effects in Film Production
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Reliability, Infocom Technologies and Optimization (Trends and Future Directions) (ICRITO)
abstract: As technology continues to evolve, the realm of visual effects in film production has witnessed a significant transformation. Deepfake technology, once associated with controversial uses, has found a legitimate and innovative application within the filmmaking industry. This paper explores the integration of deepfake expertise into film production processes, focusing on its potential to revolutionize visual effects and storytelling. By harnessing deep learning algorithms, filmmakers can create hyper-realistic digital assets, seamlessly blending fiction with reality. This paper delves into the ethical considerations, creative possibilities, and technical challenges associated with the utilization of deepfake technology in filmmaking. Furthermore, it examines case studies and industry trends to provide insights into the current landscape and prospects of incorporating deep fake expertise for enhanced visual effects in film production.

articleTitle: Cloud-Based Passenger Experience Management in Bus Fare Ticketing Systems Using Random Forest Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Reliability, Infocom Technologies and Optimization (Trends and Future Directions) (ICRITO)
abstract: Sustainable urban mobility requires optimizing public transit passenger experiences. This system integrates cloud technologies and the Random Forest algorithm with bus fare ticketing systems to improve efficiency and customer pleasure. Cloud systems provide real-time data processing for price structure and route optimization in research. Cloud computing lets transportation providers quickly adjust to shifting demand, enhancing service dependability and responsiveness. The Random Forest algorithm is integrated into ticketing procedures to estimate passenger demand and optimize prices. Historical ridership data, weather, and special events are used to provide reliable fare estimates and suggestions using machine learning. This case study shows that the suggested approach improves passenger experience, waiting times, and system efficiency in a metropolitan transport network. Scalable, cloud-based infrastructure adapts to different transportation system sizes and configurations. Findings show that cloud computing and machine learning algorithms may make public transportation systems more responsive and passenger-centric. As cities seek smarter, more environmentally friendly transportation solutions, such breakthrough technology offers potential for public transit.

Index Terms: Accuracy Of The Random Forest Model

articleTitle: Leveraging Blockchain in Labor-Intensive Jobs
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Reliability, Infocom Technologies and Optimization (Trends and Future Directions) (ICRITO)
abstract: Blockchain technology stores information electronically in digital format. Peer to peer transfer of digital is allowed which means without any third party involvement. It was first developed for Bitcoin. The interest in this technology has been increasing since the idea came up in 2008. The explanation for the interest in this technology is its attributes that offer security, anonymity and integrity with no third-party association on top of effects of the deals, and so it creates attention-grabbing analysis areas, especially from the angle of specialized challenges and limitations. Our effort involves a systematic investigation aimed at gathering all relevant research on blockchain technology. Our idea for this research is to understand the current exploration, challenges and unborn directions regarding this technology in different sectors from a specialized perspective.

articleTitle: From Athens to Rio: A Comprehensive Data Analysis and Visualization of 120 Years of Olympic History
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Reliability, Infocom Technologies and Optimization (Trends and Future Directions) (ICRITO)
abstract: The Olympic games are considered one of the most prestigious and renowned games across the globe. The first modern Olympics was held in Athens in 1896 and since then all the countries and their players have shown keen interest in reaching till Olympics. This paper presents an analysis of 120 years of Olympic history, from the first modern Olympics in Athens in 1896 to Rio in 2016. The study aims to provide insights into the evolution of Olympic participation, performance, and trends across various disciplines and nations through data visualization techniques. The data used in the analysis was sourced from the official Kaggle datasets, which include information on sportspersons, events, and outcomes from every Olympic Games held from 1896 to 2016. The visualizations were created using advanced data visualization tools such as Tableau, and R Programming. The results of the study provide insights into the changing patterns of Olympic participation, success rates, and the dominance of certain nations over time. The study also highlights the impact of historical events, technological advancements, and other factors on Olympic performance. Overall, this study provides valuable insights into the evolution of Olympic history, and the research findings can be useful for athletes, coaches, sports analysts, and policymakers to gain a good understanding of the Olympic landscape and to make informed decisions in the future.

articleTitle: Supervised Machine Learning in Cardiology: A Predictive Model for Heart Disease
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Reliability, Infocom Technologies and Optimization (Trends and Future Directions) (ICRITO)
abstract: One of the worst diseases in the world, heart disease takes a great toll on lives every year. In order to treat this potentially fatal illness, a tool or gadget must be practical, accurate, and dependable. This will allow for prompt detection or prediction, which will lead to efficient treatment and a decline in death rates. The heart is the most important organ in the human body, second only to the brain, and it is vital to the circulation of blood to all organs. A swift and accurate diagnostic method is imperative to mitigate the high mortality associated with cardiac disorders. Predicting the incidence of these disorders holds paramount importance in the medical domain. In the contemporary era, machine learning techniques prove invaluable for predicting and automating the interpretation of extensive and intricate datasets in various fields, including medicine. This research introduces a statistical model for heart disease, aiding medical examiners and cardiac practitioners in forecasting based on fundamental aspects of a patient's health history. The model, constructed using a Decision Tree, achieves an impressive accuracy of approximately 97%. The crucial functions of machine learning, data analytics, and data mining highlight how important these technologies are to improving the diagnosis and treatment of cardiac disorders.

articleTitle: Multimodal Sentiments: Unraveling Text and Emoji Dynamics Through Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Reliability, Infocom Technologies and Optimization (Trends and Future Directions) (ICRITO)
abstract: The growth of the internet has made it possible for people to use text messaging programs to communicate and share their thoughts about everyday activities as well as regional and national events. This overview examines how text mining is developing, with a focus on sentiment analysis and the newly-emerging discipline of emotion detection. It primarily focuses on the use of deep learning for code-mixed or Hinglish languages in sentiment analysis and emotion identification. This research looks at study designs, state-of-the-art models at the moment, and how well deep learning interprets data with mixed text and emojis. Insights into modern sentiment analysis are sought by shedding light on the complex interplay between textual and visual clues, with a particular emphasis on developmental stages, obstacles, and future prospects. The study provides direction for further study and advancement in the areas of multimodal sentiment analysis and emotion recognition in Hinglish or code mixed data. To further improve our comprehension of this field, a bibliometric analysis is also carried out to pinpoint the most pertinent sources, trends, and geographic patterns.

articleTitle: Firefighter Skill Advancement through IoT-Enabled Virtual Reality and CNN-Based Training
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Reliability, Infocom Technologies and Optimization (Trends and Future Directions) (ICRITO)
abstract: To maintain the safety and efficacy of firefighters in various circumstances, modern firefighting necessitates constantly improving skills and training techniques. Utilizing the Internet of Things (IoT), virtual reality (VR), and convolutional neural networks (CNN), this paper details a novel method for training firefighters. The proposed system collects real-time data on ambient variables, equipment state, and firefighter biometrics via integrating IoT sensors into firefighting equipment and training settings. Using this information, it can develop lifelike VR training simulations of difficult and potentially dangerous scenarios. To make the training settings more realistic and malleable, CNN-based algorithms are used to assess the data. The capacity to simulate a wide variety of firefighting situations, customize training difficulty depending on individual and team performance, and provide instant feedback and performance metrics to trainees are all major benefits of this method. The method also allows teachers to check in and evaluate their learners remotely, improving instruction quality. An IoT-enabled VR and CNN-based training technique has shown promising preliminary results in pilot trials, suggesting it might greatly enhance firefighter competence, situational awareness, and decision-making ability. Because of this, it has the potential to completely alter the way firefighters are informed and prepared for the ever-changing dangers users may encounter on the job.

articleTitle: IoT-Based Smart Pharmacies for Optimizing Stock Management with Long Short-Term Memory Model
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Reliability, Infocom Technologies and Optimization (Trends and Future Directions) (ICRITO)
abstract: This research presents a new method for optimizing pharmaceutical inventory management using a combination of Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) and Internet of Things (IoT) technologies. Problems with overstocking or stockouts, caused by inefficient traditional methods of stock management, may drive up expenses and leave customers unhappy. It provides a method that makes use of IoT devices to track inventory levels, sales trends, and other pertinent metrics in real-time. After that, the LSTM model is used to examine the data and make accurate predictions about stock needs in the future. The LSTM model allows for proactive stock replenishment decision-making by continually learning from previous data, thereby adapting to shifting demand patterns. It shows that our suggested approach optimizes stock levels, reduces inventory holding costs, and improves customer satisfaction via simulated studies and real-world deployments. Modern pharmacies may improve their operational efficiency and stock management procedures by integrating the IoT with LSTM. This approach is both scalable and efficient.

articleTitle: Comparator Based Envelope Tracking for RF PA Using FinFET
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Reliability, Infocom Technologies and Optimization (Trends and Future Directions) (ICRITO)
abstract: Energy efficient operation of power amplifiers (PAs) and thus preserving the battery charge for longer time is a growing concern for mobile devices without sacrificing linearity. The efficiency enhancement in radio frequency (RF) PAs is influenced by the supply modulator in the envelope tracking (ET) design. This paper presents the design of a FinFET based comparator that will form a base for designing a multilevel supply modulator that can trackthe RF input signal linearly and more precisely. A single-bit comparator has been designed that works at 3.5 GHz frequency with a minimal rise-time propagation delay of approximately 0.4 ps. The RF input signal strength is compatible with the comparator's swing of 0 - 1 V. A multilevel supply modulator design can significantly improve the power efficiency of RF P A resulting in extended battery life.

articleTitle: Drowsiness Detection for Aviation, Maritime and Land Security Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Reliability, Infocom Technologies and Optimization (Trends and Future Directions) (ICRITO)
abstract: This proposed approach uses image processing and the Python programming language to create an automatic sleepiness detection approach for a person. The objective of this proposed system is to develop an algorithm that can reliably gauge a person's ocular sleepiness under various circumstances by using real-time grayscale photographs. The person will be observed by the system as it scans their face and eyelids for hypovigilance, which is a precursor to tiredness. To properly determine the person's level of sleepiness, the suggested approach will entail three steps: feature selection, eye-pair state detection, and decision making. The algorithm will learn the characteristics that discriminate between the two states by being trained on a collection of photos of both tired and awake drivers and security personnels. To identify sleepiness in persons, facial feature recognition algorithms will also be employed, with an emphasis on the eye pair. Images will be taken with a mounted camera. For the system to successfully be integrated into current person assistance systems, it will be measured on how well it is able to identify tiredness. The research's importance stems from its ability to increase safety by identifying person sleepiness, a major contributing factor to accidents and security breaches.

articleTitle: IoT-Based Smart Water Management System with Notification and Real-Time Data Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Reliability, Infocom Technologies and Optimization (Trends and Future Directions) (ICRITO)
abstract: The device we offer is an IoT device that has an essential and effective way to analyze, control, and monitor water usage in industrial and domestic environments, notifying the increasing global concern regarding scarcity of water. With the help of a very easy-to-use mobile application, users can establish a personalized daily limit and get warnings and alerts when they begin to allocate their consumption. This application is beneficial for users to develop healthy water habits, and it offers extensive data on weekly, monthly, and annual consumption of all three types of water. Besides personal uses, this device promises to advocate community cooperation by exchanging information and trying to promote sustainable water management. This paper aims to explore the creation, application, and significant effects of IoT devices and consider the potential they hold to transform water-saving techniques completely.

articleTitle: Perspectives on the Future of Agriculture and Recent Developments in Agricultural Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Reliability, Infocom Technologies and Optimization (Trends and Future Directions) (ICRITO)
abstract: The globe is generating top frameworks or user-friendly systems to assist people, and agriculture is one of the most significant sectors where extensive and advanced study has been developed. This article emphasizes the significance of agriculture in computer science and engineering, as well as how modern technologies such as ML, IoT, Big Data, and Cyber are influencing agriculture. A thorough analysis was done and discussed, which describes certain existing frameworks and procedures in the agriculture industry from 2020 to 2023. This study discusses how top technologies such as ML, IoT, Big data and mining, and cyber-based methodologies may be used in agriculture, as well as possible future consequences. This research also addresses current frameworks and crucial elements to incorporate from the research point of view to aid farmers in improving their agricultural practices, production, and other factors. Integration of current technologies may be of great assistance in increasing the efficiency and performance of existing frameworks and forthcoming systems because it can provide numerous benefits and security for agricultural assistance in which few integrated technologies have been mentioned.

articleTitle: Cotton Plant Disease Detection and Prevention Using Deep Learning and Image Processing
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Reliability, Infocom Technologies and Optimization (Trends and Future Directions) (ICRITO)
abstract: One of the most important aspects of the agricultural economy is the production of cotton, which is threatened by diseases that lower crop quality and yield. Conventional techniques for diagnosing diseases are frequently subjective and labor-intensive. This paper presents a novel method for the automatic detection and prevention of cotton plant diseases that makes use of deep learning techniques. A convolutional neural network (CNN) model is trained using a dataset that includes various photos of both healthy and sick cotton plants. The suggested model offers a dependable and time-efficient solution by exhibiting high accuracy in differentiating between different diseases. Moreover, proactive disease detection is made possible by the integration of real-time monitoring systems, such as drones fitted with high-resolution cameras. Early detection lessens the need for broadspectrum antibiotics by enabling the prompt application of preventive measures, such as targeted therapies. Finally, we conduct a comprehensive computational analysis of eight cutting-edge object detection algorithms on the cotton plant dataset to identify diseases on the leaves and seven cutting-edge classification algorithms on the cotton plant datasets to determine if a leaf has a disease or not. computed results indicate that it has a high degree of object detection accuracy.

articleTitle: User-Centric Drink Customization with Cloud-Powered Collaborative Filtering with Raspberry Pi Integration
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Reliability, Infocom Technologies and Optimization (Trends and Future Directions) (ICRITO)
abstract: This paper proposes an approach for user-centric drink customization by combining Raspberry Pi technology with cloud-powered collaborative filtering. By using collaborative filtering algorithms housed in cloud architecture, the proposed solution seeks to improve the beverage customization experience. A specialized Raspberry Pi interface allows users to input their preferences and comments, which are automatically included in the collaborative filtering mechanism. With the help of this cloud-based system, user data can be processed and analyzed in real time, enabling personalized drink suggestions. Adding Raspberry Pi devices to a system makes it more responsive and makes data processing more localized, which is great for users. The combination of Raspberry Pi with cloud-powered collaborative filtering shows that it can provide a highly customized and adaptable drink experience. This study adds to the growing body of knowledge in cloud-based collaborative filtering and Internet of Things (IoT) applications, and it provides a potential way to improve customer happiness in the beverage business.

articleTitle: MOOT-AlexNet: A Versatile Framework for Brain Tumor Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Reliability, Infocom Technologies and Optimization (Trends and Future Directions) (ICRITO)
abstract: The precise and prompt identification of brain tumors is needed for effective treatment and the overall health of patients. This research introduces an innovative method for locating tumors in MRI scans. In this research work, the integration of machine and deep learning techniques is utilised to improve the detection and categorization of brain tumors. The machine learning approach ensures precise segmentation, while the deep learning aspect contributes to the accurate classification of MRI images. In the preprocessing stage, a Median- Anisotropic filter to eliminate noise while preserving edges was proposed. For segmentation, the Morphological Opening- Assisted Otsu Threshold (MOOT) method is proposed to improve brain tumor precision. Alexnet is utilized for brain tumor MRI images classification. The experimentation involves the analysis of 600 MRI images of brain tumors from the publicly available Figshare dataset, with 60% of the dataset (360 images) allocated for training purposes and the remaining 40% (240 images) set aside for testing. The results show an impressive accuracy of 98.44%.

articleTitle: Enhancing Facility Safety for Autonomous Gas Inspection Drones Leveraging Convolutional Neural Networks and loT Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Reliability, Infocom Technologies and Optimization (Trends and Future Directions) (ICRITO)
abstract: To increase facility safety by integrating autonomous gas inspection drones with Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) and Internet of Things (loT) technologies. Due to their ability to reach difficult situations, unmanned aerial vehicles are increasingly used for gas inspection in industry. However, drone safety and gas detection accuracy remain major issues. It offers a comprehensive method that uses CNN s for real-time image analysis and classification to help the drone locate gas leaks with high accuracy. CNN is trained on a broad dataset of gas leak situations and environmental conditions. loT technology also allows the drone and centralized monitoring system to communicate in real-time for data sharing and decision-making. Our method can adjust to changing lighting and weather and discriminate between innocuous abnormalities and gas leaks. Advanced navigation algorithms let the drone traverse complicated industrial sites while avoiding obstacles and maximizing coverage. Experimental findings show the suggested technology improves facility safety by lowering gas leak reaction times and operator risk. CNNs with loT technologies increase gas leak detection and allow proactive maintenance, improving industrial facility safety and efficiency. It advances autonomous systems for industrial applications by tackling gas inspection safety problems. The suggested framework lays the groundwork for integrating innovative technology to improve autonomous gas inspection drone capabilities and safety.

articleTitle: Mitigating Denial Based Service Attacks in Heterogeneous Sensor Networks: Strategies and Solutions
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Reliability, Infocom Technologies and Optimization (Trends and Future Directions) (ICRITO)
abstract: With the development of heterogeneous sensory networks in various applications of domains for ensuring the security against denial based service (DoS) attacks will become a paramount. In this research study, a proposal of a novel system named SecureSenseGuard(SSG) for effectively detecting DoS attacks in heterogeneous sensor networks. SecureSenseGuard(SSG) leveraging the Decision Tree (DT) algorithm augmented with Recursive type Features Elimination (RFE) for achievinga robust and efficient attack detection. The proposed system may operate by first Collection of data from diverged sensors within the network. The data, representing various network attributes, are then preprocessed and fed into the DT algorithm for classifications process. RFE will be employed as a feature selection techniques to enhance the performance of DT algorithm by iterative process for removing less relevant features, thus improving in detection accuracy and reducing computational overhead. The proposed system SecureSenseGuard(SSG) will offer several advantages over existing approaches. By employing DT, it will provide interpretable and transparent decision rules for facilitating understanding and trust in the detection process. Moreover, the integration of RFE will enhance the system's scalability and adaptability for dynamic network environments. To evaluate the effectiveness of SecureSenseGuard(SSG) an extensive experiment may be conducted by using various ranges of datasets and synthetic attack scenarios. The Results demonstrate that SecureSenseGuard(SSG) achieved high detection rates. while maintaining a low false alarm rate, outperforming traditional approaches. Overall, SecureSenseGuard(SSG) may present a promising solution in mitigating DoS attacks in heterogeneous sensory networks by offering a balance between detection accuracy, interpretability, and computational efficiency.

articleTitle: Design of Triangle-Shaped Ground Multiband MIMO Antenna for X-BandM-B, K-BandM-B (Partial) and Satellite Uplink/Downlink Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Reliability, Infocom Technologies and Optimization (Trends and Future Directions) (ICRITO)
abstract: A square-shaped Multi-Band (M-B) antenna with Multiple I/P Multiple O/P (MIMO) functionality is introduced for satellite application bands and microwave bands. A square radiating patch in a square shape with a Ctype slot, featuring dimensions of 30 × 16 mm2 designed on FR4 substrate connected through a 50Ω feeding line. The design aims to enhance isolation and achieve resonance within specified frequency bands. The integration of a triangularshaped stub onto the rectangular ground contributes to a wide bandwidth, catering to applications such as satellite uplink/downlink frequency <inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">M-B</inf> (7.25 - 7.75 GHz & 7.90 - 8.40 GHz), X-Band <inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">M-B</inf> (8.0 – 12.0 GHz), and partial K-Band <inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">M-B</inf> (18.5 – 22.5 GHz). Applications of such achieved bands for monitoring weather, defence tracking purposes, radar systems etc. The antenna exhibits good isolation and maintains a low correlation with connected grounds, which is crucial for optimal performance. Orthogonal positioning of the radiating patch reduces coupling and improves diversity performance. Moreover, the antenna's MIMO diverse properties, including impedance bandwidth, Envelope Correlation Coefficient<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">M-B</inf> (ECC<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">M-B</inf>), Total Active Reflection Coefficient<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">M-B</inf> (TARC<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">M-B</inf>), Diversity Gain<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">M-B</inf> (DG<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">M-B</inf>), Channel Capacity Loss<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">M-B</inf> (CCL<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">M</inf>B), Radiation Characteristics, and peak gain, are thoroughly analyzed. The proposed design demonstrates a ECC<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">M-B</inf> < 0.3 & a peak gain <inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">M-B</inf> of 2-4 dBi across a broad bandwidth of 2-24 GHz. The developed structure exhibits improved isolation, operates efficiently over a wide frequency range, and maintains a compact form factor without compromising diversity performance.

articleTitle: Anomaly Detectionin Network Traffic Scenarios by Resampling and Majority Voting with Concept Drift: A Hybrid Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Reliability, Infocom Technologies and Optimization (Trends and Future Directions) (ICRITO)
abstract: Addressing data imbalance is a critical difficulty in the setting of a heavily skewed dataset because the dominant class disproportionately influences classifier accuracy, especially when inadequate data impede the learning of minority class characteristics. For multi-class cases, traditional binary classification approaches are inadequate. The suggested architecture uses a Weighted Majority Voting Classifier (WMVC), noise cleaning, limited under-sampling, and oversampling to overcome this. One important step is to set an average class size limit by dividing the entire sample number by the number of classes. One or more majority classes receive Random Under sampling, all minority classes receive an up sample using the Adaptive Synthetic Sampling Approach, and noise reduction is achieved via Tomek Link. The resulting WMVC is contrasted with Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) classifiers, XGBoost, and six additional ensemble techniques by utilizing tree-based ensemble algorithms. Comparative study shows that balanced data performs better than unbalanced data. WMVC significantly beats CNN, XGBoost, and the other ensemble methods, and it improves performance for difficult minority classes while successfully decreasing classifier bias towards the majority class.

articleTitle: Examining the Role of Webrtc in Enabling Real-Time Communication Security
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Reliability, Infocom Technologies and Optimization (Trends and Future Directions) (ICRITO)
abstract: The requirement for secure and efficient remote work solutions has been increased by the Covid-19 outbreak. One potential technology for this purpose is WebRTC, which allows real-time communication within web browsers without the need to install plugins. Peer-to-peer multimedia communication across different devices is made simpler by it. This includes phone calls, data sharing, and screen sharing. Because WebRTC enables web-based platforms to provide communication functions comparable to those of programs like Skype, it has the potential to close the gap between web and native applications. Web-based learning and collaboration environments can benefit from additional features and capabilities through its integration with established communication protocols such as SIP. However, security and privacy issues must be carefully considered while incorporating WebRTC. In this paper, we provide a technical overview, highlighting the aspects of integrating WebRTC with privacy and security-two critical internet technologies.

articleTitle: Translation Systems: A Synoptic Survey of Deep Learning Approaches and Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Reliability, Infocom Technologies and Optimization (Trends and Future Directions) (ICRITO)
abstract: Within artificial intelligence, deep learning is a subset that emulates the information processing mechanism of the human brain. allowing machines to learn and make decisions on their own. This technology has revolutionized the field of language translation. Deep learning models analyze vast amounts of linguistic data, allowing visualization of context, and idiomatic expressions. This results in translations that read more naturally and capture the true essence of the source text. In order to accomplish the goal of higher accuracy, this study explores a variety of methodologies, including rule-based, neural-based, hybrid-based, and statistical-based machine translation systems, along with associated pre-processing strategies. It details the process of data collection, pre-processing, model building, training, and evaluation. The paper concludes by highlighting its key contribution in the field.

articleTitle: Technological Synergy in Agriculture: A Federated Learning CNNs Against Banana Leaf Diseases
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Reliability, Infocom Technologies and Optimization (Trends and Future Directions) (ICRITO)
abstract: Following the advancements in agricultural AI, combining federated learning with CNNs represents an innovative solution for addressing banana leaf disease. This study investigates the detection and classification of five distinct banana leaf diseases based on information provided by five clients. The federated learning model offers a privacy-preserving yet collaborative approach for data analytics critical to effectively analysing sensitive agricultural information from different regions. This approach has proven its effectiveness in our experimental results. The five clients' (eq_1 to eq_5) performance metrics reveal an apparent increase in the accuracy of disease classification. For each client, precise calculations were made for all metrics of precision, recall, F1-score support and accuracy. The comparison began with eq_1, showing the precision, recall, F1-score and accuracy values of 97% and 94.26%, respectively; their sum was also obtained at this level (Figure S3). However, these metrics consistently increased among the clients reaching eq_5 with excellent precision accuracy score F1-score values of 97.40<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>. In addition, macro-level, micro-level, and weighted average analyses gave more in-depth insights into the model's performance. In eq one, the averages were macro-90.68<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>, weighted - 91,74% and micro - 91:32%. The averages demonstrated a steadily increasing trajectory up to 97.40% for macro, 97.35 % for weighted and micro averages in eq_5. To conclude, this research shows the possibility of implementing federated learning with CNN in precision agriculture. It opens up new promising horizons for collaborative agricultural data analysis, bringing us closer to more efficient and rational banana disease control.

articleTitle: Innovating Cricket Dynamics: A CNN-SVM Approach to Bowling Movements
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Reliability, Infocom Technologies and Optimization (Trends and Future Directions) (ICRITO)
abstract: The report presents a detailed methodology involving convolutional neural networks (CNN) and support vector machines (SVM), which are used to label predefined cricket bowling actions (five types) through training. Every class's error is mathematically expressed as the width, area, and total circumference error of an ellipse in each class. The accuracy, recall, and F1 measures at the training stage are estimated to be 87.24%, 92.34%, and 89.72%, respectively. Influenza cases have been seen 496 times, representing 14<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup> of the data set and 97% accuracy. Class 2 is precise in 90,56%, recall in 93,83%, and F1-score is 92,17%. This is 583 samples out of 615, representing 16.09%, with the accuracy being 97%. Class 3 went well, with excellent memory performance of 97.91% recall percentage, 93.86% precision, and an F1 score of 0.9584. The report emphasizes several different tools intended to characterize the presented performance of the Model. The macro average accuracy is 92.83, recall is 93.62, and F1 - score is 93.17, with equal weight given to all classes. The weighted average, the so-called weighted average, builds on the class imbalance by weighting each class relative to the support it gets, and the accuracy is 93.63%, recall is 93.51%, and F1 score is 93.52%. This system is highly accurate regarding the overall mix of the cases rightly predicted, which comes at 93.51048951%.

articleTitle: The Large Action Model: Pioneering the Next Generation of Web and App Engagement
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Reliability, Infocom Technologies and Optimization (Trends and Future Directions) (ICRITO)
abstract: In the digital realm, constant attempts are made to enhance system performance and user engagement. The Large Action Model's (LAM's), a whole architecture with the power to fundamentally alter the online and application interface environments, is at the forefront of innovation. The intricate structure of LAM is examined in this work, highlighting its formidable mathematical building blocks and its potential to revolutionize digital interactions. LAM's blends theoretical brilliance with practicality via its innovative approach to modeling user behavior and system dynamics. The research thoroughly dissects the fundamental components of LAM's, emphasizing how crucial it is for optimizing backend operations. The study demonstrates how LAM's may significantly increase operational effectiveness and user engagement by evaluating its impact on important performance metrics via a rigorous analytical process. The results of the research demonstrate the revolutionary nature of LAM's and its role as the engine of an unprecedented era of the digital connection. The research subtly casts doubt on the broader ramifications of LAM's, suggesting that it may change the laws governing operational resilience and user happiness in the digital age.

Author Keywords: Large Language Models to Large Action Models

articleTitle: Harnessing the Power of CNN -SVM for Kidney Disease Classification: A Comprehensive Study
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Reliability, Infocom Technologies and Optimization (Trends and Future Directions) (ICRITO)
abstract: This study presents an innovative classification of kidney diseases. The stated method utilizes a hybrid model that integrates CNN and Support Vector Machines. The main goal of this study is to enhance the precision and efficiency of medical image processing in the early detection and classification of kidney diseases. A large data set was used to train and test the suggested model. The test results show that the CNN-SVM hybrid model performs well, with over 97% accuracy and recall rates across all classes. This dilemma has arisen as a result of the hybrid model. Another idea that underlines this fact is the accuracy of 99% overall, which shows the model can catch situations well. The findings presented in this article imply that the hybrid method can be a useful tool for nephrologists. This method is a reliable instrument in the diagnosis and characterization of early stages. As a result, the present study has made some contribution to medical image analysis tool development and there is hope that patient renal outcomes will improve.

articleTitle: AirGuard AI: Revolutionizing Air Cargo Inspection through Pygame and YOLOv8 Simulation
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Reliability, Infocom Technologies and Optimization (Trends and Future Directions) (ICRITO)
